questions.prompt: Frequency is the number of oscillations per…
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz: oscillations per second.

questions.prompt: Wavelength is the distance between…
options: A crest and the next trough only
Adjacent points in phase, such as consecutive crests
The source and the end of the medium
questions.explanation: Wavelength is one complete spatial cycle.

questions.prompt: Which equation links wave speed, frequency and wavelength?
questions.explanation: A wave travels one wavelength per oscillation period.

questions.prompt: At fixed wave speed, increasing frequency makes wavelength…
questions.explanation: λ = v/f, so f and λ are inversely related at fixed speed.

questions.prompt: Doubling the amplitude of an ideal linear wave necessarily doubles its…
questions.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium; linear-wave speed is not set by amplitude.

questions.prompt: A wave has frequency 2 Hz and wavelength 3 m. Find its speed. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 2 × 3. Result: 6 m/s.

questions.prompt: A wave has frequency 5 Hz and wavelength 2 m. Find its speed. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 5 × 2. Result: 10 m/s.

questions.prompt: A wave has frequency 4 Hz and wavelength 0.5 m. Find its speed. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 4 × 0.5. Result: 2 m/s.

questions.prompt: A wave has frequency 10 Hz and wavelength 0.4 m. Find its speed. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 10 × 0.4. Result: 4 m/s.

questions.prompt: A wave has frequency 1.5 Hz and wavelength 4 m. Find its speed. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 1.5 × 4. Result: 6 m/s.

questions.prompt: In a transverse wave, particles oscillate…
questions.explanation: Transverse means at right angles to the propagation direction.

questions.prompt: In a longitudinal wave, particles oscillate…
questions.explanation: Compressions and rarefactions travel through the medium.

questions.prompt: Sound in air is normally…
options: A wave that needs no medium
questions.explanation: Air pressure and particle motion vary along the propagation direction.

questions.prompt: A marked particle in a travelling wave typically…
options: Travels permanently to the far end
questions.explanation: Energy propagates while particles execute local oscillations in this model.

questions.prompt: Which distance is one wavelength in a longitudinal wave?
options: Compression centre to nearest rarefaction centre
From one compression centre to the next compression centre
The total spring length in every case
questions.explanation: Consecutive matching compressions are in phase and one wavelength apart.

questions.prompt: A marked spring particle oscillates at 2 Hz. What is its period? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: T = 1/f = 1/2. Result: 0.5 s.

questions.prompt: A marked spring particle oscillates at 4 Hz. What is its period? Give the closest value.
A marked spring particle oscillates at 5 Hz. What is its period? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: T = 1/f = 1/5. Result: 0.2 s.

questions.prompt: A marked spring particle oscillates at 8 Hz. What is its period? Give the closest value.
A marked spring particle oscillates at 10 Hz. What is its period? Give the closest value.
Higher sound frequency generally means higher…
options: Sound speed in the same air automatically
questions.explanation: Pitch relates primarily to frequency.

questions.prompt: Larger pressure amplitude at fixed frequency generally produces…
questions.explanation: Loudness also depends on perception and frequency, but increasing amplitude at fixed conditions increases sound intensity.

questions.prompt: Why can sound not travel through an ideal vacuum?
options: There is no material medium to transmit pressure disturbances
questions.explanation: Mechanical sound waves need particles to transmit the disturbance.

questions.prompt: In echo ranging, why divide the sound travel distance by two?
options: The wall halves the wave speed
The pulse travels out and back
questions.explanation: The measured delay is the round-trip time.

questions.prompt: Increasing the source amplitude but keeping frequency and air conditions fixed changes which microphone-trace feature?
questions.explanation: Amplitude changes vertical signal size, while period stays fixed.

questions.prompt: An echo returns after 0.2 s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. How far away is the reflector? Give the closest value.
An echo returns after 0.4 s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. How far away is the reflector? Give the closest value.
An echo returns after 0.5 s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. How far away is the reflector? Give the closest value.
An echo returns after 0.8 s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. How far away is the reflector? Give the closest value.
An echo returns after 1 s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. How far away is the reflector? Give the closest value.
A siren approaching a stationary listener is heard at a frequency that is…
questions.explanation: Wavefronts are crowded ahead of a moving source.

questions.prompt: Behind a receding sound source, wavelength is…
options: Longer than for a stationary source
questions.explanation: Successive emitted fronts are farther apart behind the source.

questions.prompt: For the same air conditions, a moving source changes the sound speed relative to stationary air by…
options: No change in this ideal model
Adding its speed in every direction
questions.explanation: Source motion changes wavefront spacing; sound speed is set by the medium in this model.

questions.prompt: In the approaching-source formula f′ = fv/(v − vₛ), vₛ must be…
options: Equal to v for all examples
Below sound speed for this subsonic model
questions.explanation: This simple periodic arrival formula is used for a subsonic source and stationary listener.

questions.prompt: When the source speed becomes zero, Doppler formulas predict…
questions.explanation: Substituting vₛ = 0 gives f′ = f.

questions.prompt: A source emits 600 Hz while approaching a stationary listener at 20 m/s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. Find the heard frequency. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For a moving source and stationary observer, f′ = fv/(v − vₛ). Result: 638 Hz.

questions.prompt: A source emits 500 Hz while approaching a stationary listener at 30 m/s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. Find the heard frequency. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For a moving source and stationary observer, f′ = fv/(v − vₛ). Result: 548 Hz.

questions.prompt: A source emits 800 Hz while approaching a stationary listener at 40 m/s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. Find the heard frequency. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For a moving source and stationary observer, f′ = fv/(v − vₛ). Result: 907 Hz.

questions.prompt: A source emits 400 Hz while approaching a stationary listener at 10 m/s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. Find the heard frequency. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For a moving source and stationary observer, f′ = fv/(v − vₛ). Result: 412 Hz.

questions.prompt: A source emits 1000 Hz while approaching a stationary listener at 50 m/s. Sound speed is 340 m/s. Find the heard frequency. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For a moving source and stationary observer, f′ = fv/(v − vₛ). Result: 1.17e+03 Hz.

questions.prompt: All electromagnetic waves in vacuum share the same…
questions.explanation: In vacuum they travel at c ≈ 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.prompt: Which band has a longer wavelength than visible light?
questions.explanation: Radio frequencies are lower and wavelengths longer than visible light.

questions.prompt: Electromagnetic waves are…
options: Transverse and able to travel through vacuum
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic fields oscillate transversely and need no material medium.

questions.prompt: Which is a common infrared application?
questions.explanation: Warm objects emit infrared, useful in thermal imaging.

questions.prompt: Moving from radio to gamma along the spectrum generally means…
questions.explanation: c = fλ fixes the inverse relationship in vacuum; photon energy increases with frequency.

questions.prompt: An EM wave has vacuum frequency 1e+06 Hz. Use c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s. Find its wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: λ = c/f. Convert powers of ten carefully. Result: 300 m.

questions.prompt: An EM wave has vacuum frequency 1e+09 Hz. Use c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s. Find its wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: λ = c/f. Convert powers of ten carefully. Result: 0.3 m.

questions.prompt: An EM wave has vacuum frequency 1e+10 Hz. Use c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s. Find its wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: λ = c/f. Convert powers of ten carefully. Result: 0.03 m.

questions.prompt: An EM wave has vacuum frequency 5e+14 Hz. Use c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s. Find its wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: λ = c/f. Convert powers of ten carefully. Result: 6e-07 m.

questions.prompt: An EM wave has vacuum frequency 1e+18 Hz. Use c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s. Find its wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: λ = c/f. Convert powers of ten carefully. Result: 3e-10 m.

questions.prompt: Reflection means a wave…
options: Returns into its original medium at a boundary
questions.explanation: A reflected wave travels back into the initial medium.

questions.prompt: Diffraction is…
options: Spreading at a gap or around an obstacle
questions.explanation: Wave spreading is most obvious when gap size is comparable to wavelength.

questions.prompt: Water waves entering a slower region keep the same…
questions.explanation: The source frequency remains unchanged at a stationary boundary.

questions.prompt: Stronger spreading is expected when a gap is…
questions.explanation: Compare gap width with the wavelength.

questions.prompt: A ray entering a slower medium bends towards the normal for oblique incidence because…
options: The normal is a material barrier
Its speed changes while frequency stays fixed
questions.explanation: Refraction changes speed and direction; wavelength adjusts to preserve frequency.

questions.prompt: A water wave has wavelength 2 cm. At unchanged frequency its speed becomes 0.5 times the original. Find the new wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: At unchanged f, wavelength changes by the same factor as wave speed. Result: 1 cm.

questions.prompt: A water wave has wavelength 4 cm. At unchanged frequency its speed becomes 0.75 times the original. Find the new wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: At unchanged f, wavelength changes by the same factor as wave speed. Result: 3 cm.

questions.prompt: A water wave has wavelength 3 cm. At unchanged frequency its speed becomes 0.6 times the original. Find the new wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: At unchanged f, wavelength changes by the same factor as wave speed. Result: 1.8 cm.

questions.prompt: A water wave has wavelength 5 cm. At unchanged frequency its speed becomes 0.4 times the original. Find the new wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: At unchanged f, wavelength changes by the same factor as wave speed. Result: 2 cm.

questions.prompt: A water wave has wavelength 1.5 cm. At unchanged frequency its speed becomes 0.8 times the original. Find the new wavelength. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: At unchanged f, wavelength changes by the same factor as wave speed. Result: 1.2 cm.
